chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the one in Ihram grappling (with someone). Is it correct for him to do so? He said: It is not correct for him out of fear that an injury might hit him, or some of his hair might fall off.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is wrestling permissible for a person in Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) prohibits wrestling for one in Ihram, citing the specific risk of injury (*jirah*) or hair loss as the primary deterrents. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preserving the physical integrity required for the ritual state, where even minor bodily changes can impact the validity of Hajj or Umrah. The prohibition underscores the principle of *khawf* (fear of harm) in deriving legal rulings, ensuring the pilgrim remains in a state of ritual purity and completeness.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad in Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup>, Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam grappling (with someone). Is it correct for him to do so?’ Heasws said: ‘It is not correct for him out of fear that an injury might hit him, or some of his hair might fall off’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Amrakiy from Ali ibn Ja’far who has said the following:
“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram; if he can fight a contest. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, because he may sustain injuries or his hair may fall.’”
